feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Evidence is iterations 0 to 5. Iteration 1 (widened 12 mm row, wheel_track 0.12 m, mass 0.8 kg, score 324.07) is the reference: oval finish rate 0.70 and oval steering_oscillation 0.26. Iteration 2 showed that 16 mm sensors collapsed oval finishes to 0.00 (progress 0.59), so keep 12 mm. Iteration 3 showed that wheel_track 0.10 m with kp 4.5 cut oval finishes to 0.10 and raised oscillation to 0.33, so do not shorten the track. Iteration 4 (mass 0.6 kg) gave oval finishes 0.30 and oscillation 0.32, and iteration 5 (mass 0.7 kg) gave 0.15 finishes, so the mass-finish relation is not monotonic. The s-bend and slalom max_error sits at about 0.064 m, above the 0.06 m off-track limit, so those tracks are unlikely to complete under any of these geometries. Your candidate, the iteration 1 reference, is the right next step. Depending on the next race: if the oval finish rate is about 0.5 or more, hold this geometry and treat it as the stable base. If it is well below 0.5, the earlier result was partly seed luck, so future geometry changes should be compared on a multi-seed average before you accept them.
requested_changes: If the oval finish rate is about 0.5 or more with steering_oscillation at or below about 0.3, hold this geometry as the stable base and stop changing the sensor row, track or mass.

Do not change sensor_size from 0.012 m or reduce wheel_track below 0.12 m again. Iterations 2 and 3 both lowered the oval finish rate.
